title: Hypothermia and Cold Exposure
content:
General awareness information only - not medical advice. Hypothermia is a dangerous drop in body temperature. It can occur not just in freezing weather but any time someone is cold and wet, especially with wind, exhaustion, or immersion. Severe hypothermia is a medical emergency.

Signs to recognize (worsening as it progresses):
- Shivering, cold/pale skin, numb hands.
- Clumsiness, stumbling, slurred speech.
- Confusion, poor judgment, drowsiness.
- In severe cases shivering may STOP, and the person becomes very drowsy or unconscious - this is a serious danger sign.

General supportive measures:
- Move the person out of cold, wind, and wet if possible.
- Replace wet clothing with dry layers; insulate from the ground.
- Cover the head and neck; wrap in blankets or a sleeping bag.
- Share body heat and provide warm (not hot) sweet drinks ONLY if the person is fully alert and able to swallow.
- Handle a severely hypothermic person gently and minimize movement; rough handling can be dangerous.

Do NOT:
- Rub or massage the limbs.
- Apply direct intense heat (hot water, heating pads directly on skin).
- Give alcohol.

Warm gradually and seek professional help, especially if the person is confused, not shivering, or losing consciousness.
